Sage Green Baby Dinosaur — 5-Inch Sitting Dino with Yellow Spikes

A small sitting dinosaur, about 5 inches tall, sage green with 8 mustard-yellow triangle spikes. Designed to sit upright without support, next to a seashell and eucalyptus sprig.

Yarn: worsted sage green (~50g) and mustard yellow (~10g). Hook 4.0mm. Gauge: ~20 sc = 4 inches, but this pattern is forgiving — yours may be 4 to 6 inches and still look right.

Skill level Beginner amigurumi — magic ring, sc, inc, invisible dec
Time About 90 minutes — head/body/tail one piece, spikes separate
Size About 5" tall sitting, 7" long nose to tail — varies with tension

What this is (and isn't)

This is a hobby pattern I wrote and tested on two dinos. The round-by-round stitch counts are internally consistent and produce the shape shown. It is not professionally tech-edited, and there is no charted diagram. If you have made one amigurumi before, you will be fine. If this is your first, read the visual checks — they matter more than exact stitch numbers.

About the photos: The images in this page are AI-generated illustrations made to show each step, not photos of my hands crocheting this exact dino. They match the colors and construction but are not step-by-step WIP photos you can use to verify your work. I am keeping them because they help show the spike shape and placement, but I want to be transparent. If you need real WIP photos, message me and I can add phone photos of my next make.

Why one piece? Head, body and tail are worked continuously without cutting yarn. That avoids a wobbly head joint and reduces sewing to just spikes and limbs. The downside is you cannot easily adjust head size later — so check size after the head rounds before continuing.

Materials

  • Sage green: Worsted — I used Lily Sugar'n Cream in Sage, 50g. Any worsted cotton/acrylic with good stitch definition works. Avoid fuzzy yarn — it hides decreases.
  • Mustard yellow: Worsted — Loops & Threads Impeccable in Butterscotch, ~10g for 8 spikes.
  • Hook: 4.0mm. If you see stuffing through stitches, use 3.5mm. If your hands hurt, use 4.5mm and stuff a little less.
  • Eyes: 10mm safety eyes, or black yarn for French knots if for a child under 3.
  • Other: Tapestry needle, stitch marker, polyfill. Small seashell and eucalyptus sprig optional for display.
PartApprox sizeWhat to check visually
Head2.5" diameterRound and chubby, not pointy. Forehead should be taller than snout.
Body3" wideShould be wider than head, able to sit flat.
Tail3" longTapers to point, base lightly stuffed so tip can curve slightly.
Spikes0.75" triangles8 total, standing up, not flopping. Sewn with 2 stitches at base.

Construction overview

Order:
1. Head — MR 6 → 30, work 5 rounds straight, then start dec for neck (don't cut)
2. Body + tail — continue from neck, inc to 30, work straight, dec to tail, close
3. Spikes x8 — separate yellow triangles, pin in line down center back
4. Face — eyes, smile, blush
5. Arms x2, legs x2 — sew, check that it sits

Abbreviations

MR = magic ring (or ch 2, 6 sc in 2nd ch). sc = single crochet. inc = 2 sc in same stitch. dec = invisible decrease — front loops only of next 2 stitches, YO pull through both front loops, YO pull through 2. FO = fasten off. Work in continuous rounds, move marker each round.

Step 1: Head

Illustration 1 · Magic ring start
1Head — chubby, big forehead
Illustration: magic ring start with sage green yarn, 6 sc. Yellow triangle spikes shown beside for scale. Not a WIP photo of this exact dino — see note above.

Start with sage green. Pull MR tight so there is no hole at top.

Head — Sage Green — 4.0mm:
R1: MR, 6 sc (6)
R2: inc around (12)
R3: [sc, inc] x6 (18)
R4: [2 sc, inc] x6 (24)
R5: [3 sc, inc] x6 (30)
R6-10: sc around (30) — 5 rounds straight. Check: should be about 2.5" diameter, cup-shaped, not flat.
R11: [3 sc, dec] x6 (24) — this is the neck, do NOT fasten off, continue to body.

If your head looks pointy, you may have missed increases. Count should be 30 before the straight rounds. If it looks very small (2"), your tension is tight — that is okay, your finished dino will be about 4" tall.

Step 2: Body and tail — one piece from head

Illustration 2 · Body and tail one piece
2Body and tail — continuous, no cut
Illustration: body about 3" wide and tail 3" long, one piece from head. Flat bottom helps it sit.
Body + Tail — Sage Green:
R12: [3 sc, inc] x6 (30) — chubby body
R13-18: sc around (30) — 6 rounds. Check: body should be slightly wider than head, about 3" wide.
R19: [3 sc, dec] x6 (24) — hips
R20-22: sc around (24)
Tail: R23 [2 sc, dec] x6 (18), R24-25 sc (18), R26 [sc, dec] x6 (12), R27-28 sc (12), R29 [sc, dec] x3 (9), R30 sc (9), R31 dec to 6, close. Stuff body firmly as you go. Tail: stuff base only, leave tip lightly stuffed so it can curve slightly up.

Finished: about 5" tall sitting, 7" nose to tail. To test sitting, place on table — legs and tail tip should all touch table. If it tips, add a little more stuffing to bottom or flatten legs.

Step 3: Yellow spikes — 8 triangles

Illustration 3 · Yellow spikes
3Spikes — 8 small triangles
Illustration: 8 yellow triangles, about 0.75" tall. Real spikes are crocheted flat, not stuffed.
Spikes x8 — Mustard Yellow:
R1: MR yellow 4 sc (4)
R2: [sc, inc] x2 (6)
R3: sc around (6), flatten to triangle, FO leave 8" tail. No stuffing. Make 8.

Placement — do this by eye: Pin all 8 in a straight line down center back, from top of head to tail tip. Spacing should look even — about 0.75" to 1" between bases. 3 on head, 5 down back/tail is a guide; if yours looks better with 3-4 on head, use that. Sew each with 2 stitches at base so it stands up. If spikes flop, you sewed only 1 stitch or left tail too loose.

Step 4: Face

Illustration 4 · Face placement
4Eyes, smile, blush
Illustration: eye placement guide — about one eye-width apart, slightly to sides, not front-center. Smile small and centered below.

Eyes: Place between R7-8 of head. Distance: about one eye-width gap between eyes — roughly 5 stitches, but check from front. If 5 looks wide on your head, use 4. Add a tiny white highlight stitch at top edge of each eye with white yarn if you like.

Smile: Small U shape, centered below eyes, about R10-11, about 2 stitches wide. Embroider with black yarn.

Blush: Two small horizontal pink stitches on cheeks, below and slightly outside eyes. Optional but adds friendliness. Use pink yarn, not marker — marker fades.

Step 5: Arms and legs

Illustration 5 · Arms and legs
5Arms and legs — small and lightly stuffed
Illustration: arms about 1", legs about 1.25", lightly stuffed so they flop slightly rather than stick out stiff.
Arms x2 — Sage: MR 6 sc, R2-4 sc (6) — 3 rounds, ~1" long, lightly stuff pinch, FO
Legs x2 — Sage: MR 6 sc, R2 [sc, inc] x3 (9), R3-5 sc (9), R6 dec to 6, FO lightly stuff

Placement: Pin first. Arms at mid-body height, a few stitches out from belly center, angled slightly forward. Legs at bottom front, flat bottoms touching table, gap between them about width of tail base. Sew and re-check sitting. Light stuffing is intentional — heavily stuffed limbs stick out like airplane wings.
